topics.title: 4.1 State Fundamentals with useState
topics.description: Learn state declarations, updater functions, and re-rendering lifecycles.
topics.lessonMarkdown:
# 4.1 State Fundamentals with useState ## What is state? Props are values given to a component. State is information a component remembers and can update over time. Examples: - counter value - selected tab - open/closed menu - form input - logged-in user - cart quantity --- ## 1. Importing `useState` ```jsx import { useState } from "react"; ``` Then: ```jsx const [count, setCount] = useState(0); ``` This gives you two things: ```text count → current value setCount → updater function ``` --- ## 2. First example ```jsx function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); return ( ); } ``` Initially: ```text count = 0 ``` After one click: ```text count = 1 ``` React renders again. --- ## 3. State is preserved between renders A normal local variable does not work like React state: ```jsx function App() { let count = 0; function increase() { count += 1; } return ; } ``` Updating `count` does not tell React to render a new screen. State does: ```jsx const [count, setCount] = useState(0); ``` --- ## 4. Updater functions When the next state depends on the previous state, use the updater form: ```javascript setCount(previous => previous + 1); ``` This is especially useful when several updates happen close together. ```jsx setCount(previous => previous + 1); setCount(previous => previous + 1); ``` The updates are based on the queued previous values. --- ## 5. State can be many types Number: ```javascript const [count, setCount] = useState(0); ``` String: ```javascript const [name, setName] = useState(""); ``` Boolean: ```javascript const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); ``` Array: ```javascript const [items, setItems] = useState([]); ``` Object: ```javascript const [profile, setProfile] = useState({ name: "", level: 1 }); ``` --- ## 6. Updating object state Do not overwrite unrelated fields accidentally. Bad: ```javascript setProfile({ level: 2 }); ``` Good: ```javascript setProfile(previous => ({ ...previous, level: 2 })); ``` --- ## 7. Updating array state Add: ```javascript setItems(previous => [...previous, newItem]); ``` Remove: ```javascript setItems(previous => previous.filter(item => item.id !== id) ); ``` Update: ```javascript setItems(previous => previous.map(item => item.id === id ? { ...item, done: true } : item ) ); ``` --- ## 8. State does not update the variable immediately This is an important concept. ```javascript setCount(count + 1); console.log(count); ``` The `console.log` can still show the previous render's value. Think of the setter as requesting the next state and React then rendering again. --- ## 9. Event handlers change state ```jsx const handleIncrement = () => { setCount(previous => previous + 1); }; ``` Then: ```jsx ``` Other controls: ```jsx ``` --- ## 10. Derived values should usually stay derived Suppose state is: ```javascript const [price, setPrice] = useState(100); const taxRate = 0.08; ``` You can calculate: ```javascript const finalPrice = price * (1 + taxRate); ``` You usually do not need a second state variable just for `finalPrice`. Keep source-of-truth state minimal. --- ## Common mistakes - Calling hooks inside `if` or loops. - Mutating an array/object in state. - Replacing an object and accidentally deleting other properties. - Using state for values that can be calculated from existing state. - Using the current state value when an updater function is clearer for repeated updates. --- ## A complete beginner example ```jsx import { useState } from "react"; export default function App() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); return (

{count}

This is called a **controlled input**. --- ## 1.
